learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of eight components stands alone or depends on the rest of its resource, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** standalone-lift-test
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight components stands alone or depends on the rest of its resource, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Modular Content, Standalone Component (both defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each component the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the lift test is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A component is standalone if it has its own file. (2) A short component is always standalone. (3) A reference to another section is harmless. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging whether a component stands alone is an Evaluate-level action that applies a stated test. Eight components that differ in one detail each teach the learner to look for hidden dependencies. **Content:** The lift test, shown at all times: copy the component to a new place, and check that it makes sense without the rest, and that everything it needs comes with it. The two bins: Stands alone, and Depends on the rest. The eight components: | # | Component shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A reading that opens with a definition and uses only terms it defines. | Stands alone | It needs nothing from other sections. | | 2 | A quiz whose questions say "refer to the diagram in section 2". | Depends on the rest | The diagram is not part of the quiz. | | 3 | A simulation in its own folder with its own page, instructions, and script. | Stands alone | Everything it needs travels with it. | | 4 | A figure with its own caption and alt text but a caption that begins "as discussed above". | Depends on the rest | The caption refers to text that is not there. | | 5 | A glossary page that defines each term in full. | Stands alone | Each definition is complete. | | 6 | A section that begins "now that you have finished section 3, turn to section 4". | Depends on the rest | It assumes the reader came from section 3. | | 7 | A worked example that restates the problem, the method, and the answer. | Stands alone | It holds everything needed to follow it. | | 8 | A simulation page that loads a script from a different chapter's folder. | Depends on the rest | It breaks when moved without that folder. | **Provenance:** The components are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The test follows the chapter section "Standalone Component". **Rules:** Each component has exactly one correct bin, four per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one component and the two bins. 2. The learner places the component in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After component 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 components in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can run the lift test." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed component. **Starting State:** The first component, the lift test, and two empty bins. The question shown is "Would this still work if you copied it somewhere new?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked example lifts out the reading, the quiz, and the images from Watershed Basics, and finds that the quiz is not standalone because it refers to the river in section 2.
